descriptionAdvanced.de: Amington ist ein geschichtsträchtiger Stadtteil im Osten von Tamworth, Staffordshire, der eine harmonische Verbindung zwischen ländlichem Erbe und moderner Vorstadtentwicklung darstellt. Ursprünglich als sächsische Siedlung gegründet, wurde der Ort bereits im Domesday Book erwähnt. Die Entwicklung Amingtons wurde maßgeblich durch den Bau des Coventry-Kanals im späten 18. Jahrhundert beeinflusst, der die lokale Wirtschaft durch den Transport von Kohle und landwirtschaftlichen Erzeugnissen ankurbelte. Geografisch erstreckt sich der Stadtteil entlang des Nordufers des Flusses Anker, was ihm grüne Korridore und beliebte Naherholungsgebiete beschert. Die St. Editha’s Kirche, ein prominentes Bauwerk aus dem 19. Jahrhundert, zeugt von der Bedeutung des ehemaligen Dorfes. In den letzten Jahrzehnten hat sich Amington zu einem beliebten Wohngebiet für Pendler entwickelt, die die Nähe zu den Industriezentren der Midlands schätzen, während die Treppelwege am Kanal heute als malerische Routen für Radfahrer und Spaziergänger dienen.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Amington Tamworth egyik legrégebbi múltra visszatekintő városrésze Staffordshire-ben, amely egykor virágzó mezőgazdasági és bányászati közösség volt. A település neve a szász 'Amingtun' szóból ered, ami Aming népének faluját jelenti. A 18. század végén kiépült Coventry-csatorna alapjaiban változtatta meg a falu életét, összekötve azt a feltörekvő ipari központokkal és lehetővé téve a helyi szénbányák termelésének növelését. Az Anker-folyó völgyében fekvő terület ma is megőrizte zöld jellegét, köszönhetően a tágas közparkoknak és a csatornapart menti tanösvényeknek. Amington Hall, a klasszicista kúria, emlékeztet a terület nemesi múltjára, míg a modern lakóparkok a városrész töretlen fejlődését mutatják. A közösség központja az Amington Heath, ahol számos helyi szolgáltatás és iskola található. A természetközeli fekvés és a jó közlekedési kapcsolatok miatt Amington ma Tamworth egyik legkeresettebb lakóövezete, amely sikeresen ötvözi a kisvárosi hangulatot a nagyvárosi kényelemmel.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Amington este o suburbie dinamică a orașului Tamworth, cu o istorie ce se întinde pe mai bine de un mileniu, fiind menționată documentar încă din perioada anglo-saxonă. Situată în valea râului Anker, localitatea a evoluat de la o mică așezare feudală la un important nod industrial odată cu deschiderea canalului Coventry în 1790. Acest canal a facilitat transportul cărbunelui din bazinul carbonifer local, transformând peisajul dintr-unul pur agricol într-unul mixt. Punctul focal istoric al suburbiei este Biserica Sf. Editha, o capodoperă a arhitecturii victoriene care deservește comunitatea locală. Din punct de vedere geografic, Amington beneficiază de spații verzi extinse, precum Rezervația Naturală Hodge Lane, creată pe locul unei foste mine de argilă. Expansiunea urbană recentă a integrat Amington perfect în structura orașului Tamworth, însă locuitorii păstrează un sentiment puternic de identitate locală, celebrat prin evenimente comunitare și conservarea patrimoniului industrial legat de rețeaua națională de canale.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Amington is a historic district located on the eastern fringe of Tamworth in Staffordshire, blending ancient roots with 21st-century residential living. Recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086, it spent centuries as an agricultural parish before the arrival of the Coventry Canal in the late 1700s triggered a period of industrial expansion. The discovery of coal seams nearby led to the establishment of the Amington Colliery, which was a major employer until its closure in the early 20th century. Today, the canal remains a central feature, serving as a 'green lung' for the community and providing a peaceful environment for narrowboating and walking. The district is bounded by the River Anker to the south, which often defines the area's lush topography. Recent housing developments have significantly increased the population, but the core village feel persists around the historic parish church and the local village green. Its proximity to the M42 and the railway connections of Tamworth make it a strategic location for residents working across the West Midlands.

en: Amington is listed in the Domesday Book as 'Aminton'.
The Coventry Canal through the area was opened in 1790.
Amington Colliery closed its shafts in 1924.
St Editha's Church is a Grade II listed building completed in 1864.
Hodge Lane was designated a Local Nature Reserve in 1997.
The district is roughly 15 miles northeast of Birmingham city centre.
